terms.definition: Figures with congruent corresponding angles and proportional corresponding lengths.
A transformation from a center that multiplies distances from the center by one scale factor.
The fixed point from which dilation rays originate.
The ratio of an image length to its corresponding preimage length.
The original figure before a transformation.
The resulting figure after a transformation.
A translation, rotation, or reflection that preserves distances and angle measures.
A sequence of rigid motions and a dilation that maps one figure to a similar figure.
Vertices that occupy matching positions in two related figures.
Sides joining corresponding vertices in related figures.
Triangle similarity established by two pairs of congruent corresponding angles.
Triangle similarity established when all three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional.
Triangle similarity established by two proportional corresponding side pairs and congruent included angles.
The angle formed by the two sides being used in an SAS relationship.
An equation stating that two ratios are equal.
A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally.
Another name for the Triangle Proportionality Theorem.

terms.term: converse of the Triangle Proportionality Theorem
terms.definition: If a segment divides two sides of a triangle proportionally, that segment is parallel to the third side.
A drawing whose lengths are proportional to corresponding real lengths according to a stated scale.
A three-dimensional representation built with dimensions proportional to an actual object.
Rewriting a measurement in an equivalent unit before comparing or scaling quantities.
Finding an inaccessible length by using relationships such as similarity instead of measuring it directly.
A straight visual path between an observer and a target, often used in indirect-measurement models.
The difference between a measured or estimated value and the actual value due to instrument, setup, or observation limits.
